title: Installment Payment Plans — Plan Schedule: Down Payments and Installment Calendar
content:
Under the **Installment Payment Plans** of Cardinal Point Insurance Company, each of the six plans fixes how much of the term premium is collected up front, how many installments follow, and on which calendar the installments fall due and are invoiced. The figures below are the plan schedule for every plan.

## Schedule by plan

| Plan | Down payment, new-business term (percent of the term premium billed) | Down payment, renewal term (percent of the renewal term premium) | Installments after the down payment | First installment due (calendar months after the term effective date) | Months between installment due dates | Invoice or draft notice issued (calendar days before the due date) | Automatic draft date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan | 100 | 100 | 0 | 0 (no installments) | 0 (no further installments) | 0 | not applicable |
| Cardinal Point Two-Pay Plan | 50 | 50 | 1 | 3 | 0 (no further installments) | 20 | not applicable |
| Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan | 25 | 25 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 20 | not applicable |
| Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan | 20 | 16 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 20 | not applicable |
| Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan | 17 | 16.6 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 10 | the due date, or the next banking day |
| Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan | 17 | 16.6 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 10 | the due date, or the next banking day |

Fully earned fees charged with a new-business term are added to its down payment in full; renewal fees are added in full to the renewal down payment. The percentages above apply to premium only.

## Spreading and calendar conventions (all plans)

- **Spread of the premium after the down payment:** equal installments, each rounded to the cent, with the final installment absorbing any difference left by the rounding.
- **Due day that does not exist in a month:** the due date is the last calendar day of that month.
- **Automatic draft date:** on the two monthly draft plans the payment is drafted on the due date or, when that is not a banking day, on the next banking day. Plans billed directly have no draft date.

## Invoice lead time and the scoped current basis

The invoice lead time is the number of calendar days before the due date on which an installment invoice (or draft notice) is issued. For a draft notice on a plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term, and only for such a notice, the notice is issued that many calendar days before its due date and bills what the draft notice schedule states; the first invoice after an owner plan is moved off automatic draft to the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan at the named insured's request is issued on the move's day and billed as its own schedule states; any other invoice, a later invoice of a moved plan included, is issued the lead time before its due date and bills the installment premium, the plan's installment fee together with the certificate filing fee it bills, and every past-due amount still unpaid, its minimum due being their sum.

## Reading the schedule (hypothetical illustration)

On a hypothetical Four-Pay new-business term with a term premium billed of 900.00 and an effective date of the 31st of a month, the down payment premium is 25 percent, 225.00, and the remaining 675.00 is spread as three installments of 225.00. Installment 1 falls due one calendar month after the effective date; in a month with only 30 days it falls on the 30th, and its invoice is issued 20 calendar days before that date. The Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan has no installments at all: its down payment is the whole premium.
